text: Your skin does at least six jobs without asking you. It raises hairs, folds your fingertips, cools you down, answers the sun, holds water in, and drew a pattern on your fingers before you were born. Here is how each one works.
That was a nerve telling a muscle what to do. Your nerves run another trick in your fingertips, and you have seen it in the bath.
Wrinkled fingers, run by your nervous system. Now a job your skin does for the whole body: it cools you.
Sweat handles heat. Sunlight is another story, and your skin answers it with pigment.
That was pigment answering sunlight. Underneath it, a wall of cells and fats keeps water in.
A wall built from cells and fats, layer by layer. And on the outside of it, a pattern you have carried since before you were born.

So that is your skin, working without you. A muscle, a nerve and a hair, for goosebumps. Nerves that fold your fingertips. Sweat that cools you as it dries. Pigment that caps a cell's nucleus. A wall of bricks and fats. And a pattern drawn in waves before birth. None of it needs your permission, and most of it is going on in your skin right now.
If you just looked at your own arm, tap like and subscribe!
